text:
olivia: Quick triage note 0min: new reranker v3-int8 on web+med holdouts shows NDCG ~same but MRR -2.8 overall. Breakdown suggests the loss is concentrated in queries where top-1 and top-2 are near-duplicates.

devon: Interesting, did we change the candidate dedupe or the holdout dedupe threshold between runs? Those can hide/reveal near-duplicate swaps and blow up MRR.

olivia: No pipeline change AFAICT. Same candidate job id. But I noticed the eval harness dedupe step uses a default "jaccard_threshold"=0.65 in float run config and 0.6 in the int8 canary config (accidentally).

ravi: That difference could absolutely change MRR. If the canary dedupes more aggressively at eval time, high-quality near-duplicates might get removed differently causing top1 to look worse.

tess: Can you post the small slice table for dup vs non-dup queries?

olivia: Pasted quick csv below and uploaded full slice to s3://redwood-bench/rerank/2147484000/dedupe-slices.csv
```
model,cohort,ndcg,mrr,top1,dup_slice_mrr,nondup_mrr
float32,all-holdout,0.625,0.512,0.54,0.485,0.523
int8,all-holdout,0.623,0.498,0.50,0.452,0.508
float32,med-holdout,0.633,0.499,0.51,0.469,0.509
int8,med-holdout,0.632,0.486,0.47,0.430,0.494
```

devon: Dup-slice MRR drop is the smoking gun. Two hypotheses: 1) eval-time dedupe mismatch between runs, 2) quantization changes ranking for near-identical docs due to small score jitter and that interacts with downstream dedupe post-processing at serving.

ravi: To differentiate, run three ablations: (A) int8 with float eval-dedupe config, (B) float but eval-dedupe=0.6 to simulate canary, (C) int8 with increased scorer-smoothing (scale logits by 1.02) to reduce jitter.

tess: Also add a per-query disagreement dump limited to dup-slice where rank flip happens. That helps see if flips are meaningful or just order noise between nearly identical docs.

olivia: Kicked off the three ablations on a small 10k sample (dup-heavy). Jobs: 2147484011 (A), 2147484022 (B), 2147484033 (C). CI link: https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/2147484011

ci-bot: Job 2147484011 queued. Job 2147484022 queued. Job 2147484033 queued.

devon: FYI we should also verify candidate recall didn't change: if int8 runtime earlier pruned low-score items differently before rerank, that could change the set rereranked. Confirm pre-rerank pruning thresholds identical.

olivia: Pre-rerank pruning is identical per job metadata. I pulled example traces: both fed 100 candidates for the problem queries. The flips are within the top-10.

ravi: Good. If ablation A (int8 with float dedupe) still shows dup-slice MRR drop, it's quantization affecting fine-grained score ordering. If B (float with canary dedupe) reproduces drop, it's purely eval config mismatch. If C helps, smoothing is a potential mitigation.

tess: Also quick note for onboarding checklist: add a conserved-eval-config guard that asserts dedupe thresholds and any postprocessing flags are identical between float and canary runs. Save future headaches.

olivia: Agreed. I'll open a short PR to the harness: fail-canary-if-eval-config-diff. Ticket in GT: RERANK-3147.

devon: After ablations finish, if it's quant jitter we should consider rank-stabilization (logit smoothing or pairwise margin calibration) before shipping int8. If it's config mismatch, rollback the harness change and re-run canary.

olivia: Results ETA ~20m. Will drop per-query disagreement dump link here.

ci-bot: Job 2147484011 completed 0m ago. Logs: https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/2147484011/logs

olivia: Early peek: A (int8+float-dedupe) recovers ~1.8% MRR on dup-slice vs original int8. B (float+canary-dedupe) drops similarly to int8 baseline. C (smoothing) recovers ~1.1% on dup-slice. Seems majority is eval-config mismatch.

ravi: Great catch. Action: revert the accidental dedupe change in canary config and re-run full canary. Also keep smoothing in our checklist as a low-cost stabilizer for near-duplicate heavy workloads.

tess: I'll update rollout playbook and add a line: "check eval dedupe & candidate postprocessing parity".

olivia: Done. Re-run full canary queued (job 2147484050). Will post final numbers when ready. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
